application_credentials.description:
Nothing to add: the integration signs in through its own published Cloudflare OAuth client.

Add a credential only to use [a client of your own]({docs_oauth_clients}); it then replaces the built-in one. Create it under Manage Account → OAuth clients with redirect URL `{redirect_uri}`, grant types authorization code and refresh token, token endpoint authentication none (PKCE) and the scopes {scopes}; enter its client ID with an empty secret. The [project notes]({more_info_url}) walk through it.

user.title: Cloudflare Access
user.description:
Puts the whole hostname behind Cloudflare Access: only people with a Home Assistant account get in, and voice assistants or MCP clients sign in through Access.

Continue to sign in with Cloudflare; the consent page lists the permissions used.

Use a desktop browser: the Android companion app cannot finish the return from the consent page.

account.title: Cloudflare account
account.description: The sign-in was granted for several accounts. Choose the one whose zone serves the hostname.

api_token.title: Cloudflare API token
api_token.description: An account-level token with the permissions 'Access: Apps and Policies: Edit' and 'Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups: Read'. Stored in the config entry.

settings.title: Hostname and options
settings.description:
The gate starts off; nothing changes at the edge until you switch it on in the options.

Who gets in: every active user with an e-mail address, either as login username or as a login e-mail you give them, through the [login methods of your Zero Trust organization]({docs_identity_providers}). Currently: {allowed_users}.

Nobody can log in without an address, so at least one user needs one; the fields below appear while none has.

data.delete_objects_on_remove: Delete the Access applications when the integration is removed

data_description.hostname: The public hostname Cloudflare serves, e.g. ha.example.com.
data_description.user_id: The Home Assistant user who gets the address.
data_description.email: The address the identity provider knows this user by.
data_description.extra_bypass_paths:
Path prefixes reachable without a login, for callers that hold neither cookie nor token; each gets a [bypass policy]({docs_policies}) of its own.

Pick from what this Home Assistant serves, or type one.
data_description.client_redirect_uris:
Where a self-registering client (MCP) may be sent back to: Access [registers such a client]({docs_managed_oauth}) only for a listed URL.

Example: {example_mcp_redirect}, or {example_wildcard_redirect} for every path.

A client that asks for a client ID and secret is added under "Add OAuth client" instead.
data_description.service_token_ids: Client IDs of [Access service tokens]({docs_service_tokens}) that may pass the gate, e.g. for a script on another machine.
data_description.session_duration: How long an [Access session]({docs_session}) lasts before the person must log in again; also the lifetime of a registered client's refresh token.
data_description.delete_objects_on_remove: Off keeps the Access applications in Cloudflare after removal, e.g. to adopt them from another instance.

reauth_confirm.title: Sign in with Cloudflare again
reauth_confirm.description: Cloudflare no longer accepts the sign-in. Continue to sign in again.

init.title: Cloudflare Access for {hostname}
init.description:
Saving re-provisions the Access applications; reloading the integration does the same without a change.

Who gets in: every active user with an e-mail address, either as login username or as a login e-mail added here, through the [login methods of your Zero Trust organization]({docs_identity_providers}) (Zero Trust → Integrations → Identity providers). Currently: {allowed_users}.

A user without an address cannot log in: give one under "Add login e-mail", or [change the username]({docs_change_username}) to the address.

restart_required.title: Restart Home Assistant to accept clients authenticated by Cloudflare Access
restart_required.description: The integration was set up after the web server had started, so its authentication middleware could not be installed. Until Home Assistant is restarted, requests from token-bearing clients (Google Assistant, Alexa, MCP clients) that Cloudflare Access admitted are rejected by Home Assistant.

no_allowed_users.title: No Home Assistant user can pass the Cloudflare Access gate
no_allowed_users.description:
No active user has an e-mail address any more, so there is nobody to list in the gate's allow policy; it was left as it was.

Give a user one under "Add login e-mail" on the integration, or [change a username]({docs_change_username}) to the address.

user.title: Login e-mail
user.description:
The address Access knows a Home Assistant user by, for a user whose login username is not one (Home Assistant has no e-mail field).

It joins the gate's allow policy, and a login with it is served as this user.

data_description.user_id: The Home Assistant user who gets the address.
data_description.email: The address the identity provider knows this user by.

error.user_taken: This user already has a login e-mail.

user.title: Register an OAuth client
user.description:
For a client whose console asks for a client ID and secret: Google Home account linking, the Alexa skill, any service that cannot register itself.

Access issues the credentials from [an application of its own]({docs_saas_apps}) for the client; the next page shows them with the URLs to enter in that console. Who may link is the gate's own allow rule.

data_description.name: Anything that identifies the client to you, e.g. Google Home.
data_description.redirect_uris: The callback URL(s) the client's console shows, e.g. {example_console_redirect}.

reconfigure.title: Change the OAuth client
reconfigure.description: Saving updates the registration in Access and shows the credentials again.
